newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MEMORABLE NIGHT IN THE RAIN AS SCHALKE REACH LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEMORABLE NIGHT IN THE RAIN AS SCHALKE REACH LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Schalke of Germany reached the last eight of a European competition for the first time in 23 years on Tuesday when a last minute header from Dutchman Youri Mulder gave them a 2-0 win over Club Brugge of Belgium for a 3-2 UEFA Cup aggregate victory.
A capacity crowd of 51,000 was brought to its feet as Mulder scored to give Schalke a 2-0 win on the night after Club Brugge won the opening leg 2-1.

Martin Max -- who limped off early in the second half with a thigh strain -- opened the scoring in the ninth minute when he suddenly found himself in space 10 metres out and gave Brugge keeper Danny Verlinden no chance.
With the benefit of Michael Buesken's first leg goal, Schalke held the upper hand on the away goals rule, and contained whatever threats Brugge threw their way.
But with heavy rain falling throughout the match and the pitch muddy and slippery, Schalke could not afford to relax, but always did enough to hold the Belgians at bay.

Huub Stevens, Schalke's Dutch coach said afterwards: "We had to fight to get a result and thats what we did" while club manager Rudi Assauer enthused: "It's a milestone in the history of Schalke. Getting to the quarter-finals is sensational, we were banking on surviving just one round."

The only black mark on an otherwise memorable night for Schalke was a booking for Dutchman Johan de Kock, which was his second of the competition and will keep him out of the first leg of the quarter-final next March.
But one plus point for all concerned was that there was no repeat of the crowd violence that marred the first leg in Belgium two weeks ago.
